title: Answers to eikö possession questions with plural owners
summary: Answer negative possession questions about plural owners according to the stated fact.
prerequisiteSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
objectives: Answer negative possession questions about plural owners according to the stated fact.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Answer negative possession questions about plural owners according to the stated fact.
If the owner does have the thing, answer On. or Kyllä, on. If the owner does not have it, answer Ei ole. or Ei, ei ole. A negative question does not reverse the facts.
keyPoints: Answer negative possession questions about plural owners according to the stated fact.

examples.finnish: Eikö meillä ole autoa? — Ei, ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t we have a car? — We do not have it.
steps: meillä means “we as the owner”. The question names autoa (“a car”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The first Ei (“no”) is an optional answer particle; Ei ole. alone also denies possession.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.english: Don’t you have a game? — You do have it.
steps: teillä means “you as the owner” for a group. The question names peliä (“a game”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.finnish: Eikö heillä ole kynää? — Ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t they have a pen? — They do not have it.
steps: heillä means “they as the owner”. The question names kynää (“a pen”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.finnish: Eikö meillä ole tyynyä? — Ei, ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t we have a pillow? — We do not have it.
steps: meillä means “we as the owner”. The question names tyynyä (“a pillow”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The first Ei (“no”) is an optional answer particle; Ei ole. alone also denies possession.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.finnish: Eikö meillä ole palloa? — Kyllä, on.
examples.english: Don’t we have a ball? — Yes.
steps: Read the stated possession fact.
The owners have the thing: use on.
The optional answer word does not change the fixed verb reply.

examples.finnish: Eikö teillä ole kirjaa? — Ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t you have a book? — No.
steps: teillä identifies the plural owner in this answers to eikö possession questions with plural owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
kirjaa (“a book”) is the complete regular singular partitive: kirja + -a.
The stated fact denies possession, so reply Ei ole.

examples.finnish: Eikö teillä ole kissaa? — Ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t you have a cat? — No.
steps: teillä identifies the plural owner in this answers to eikö possession questions with plural owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
kissaa (“a cat”) is the complete regular singular partitive: kissa + -a.
The stated fact denies possession, so reply Ei ole.

examples.finnish: Eikö heillä ole koiraa? — Ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t they have a dog? — No.
steps: heillä identifies the plural owner in this answers to eikö possession questions with plural owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
koiraa (“a dog”) is the complete regular singular partitive: koira + -a.
The stated fact denies possession, so reply Ei ole.

commonMistakes: A negative question does not reverse the fact: On still confirms having the thing, and Ei ole still denies it.
Keep the reply fixed for every owner; Olemme and Emme ole describe “we are” and “we are not”, rather than possession.
Use the requested verb reply; optional Kyllä or an additional Ei does not replace on or ei ole.
